claims.decision: Scope is frozen S003, 896 logical lines, whole brief; source keyword/conformance vocabulary and citation convention are accurate.

No live fetch, no code/filesets/execution, and only cited evidence are process absence assertions. Current report consistently marks validation UNEXECUTED; acquisition/runtime history is locked, so actual process absence is not independently verified.

S003 does not fully determine the on-disk contract: it delegates Zarr encoding to an uncaptured external specification, and references other missing specifications. Namespace/version and listed keys are supported, but the completeness assertion overstates source fit.

The thin plan is directionally compatible and omits the named detailed mechanisms. This supports implementation-gap findings; several listed display choices are recommendations/options rather than format obligations, assessed separately below.

All Zarr features are admitted unless disallowed, but the assertion that no disallowance occurs anywhere in capture is false: labels have a closed integer dtype requirement and images/transforms have explicit restrictions. Unsupported-backend feedback is a valid plan implication; unbounded and largest are not established measurements.

Tools is only a pointer; captured source cannot establish actual implementation interoperability/tolerance/performance. The report correctly leaves that requested research unresolved under fixed source scope, rather than claiming incompatibility.
Local-only, read-only, no editing/export/remote/clinical interpretation and session-local display state are product boundaries; format permits other storage locations.

Metadata is attributes.ome in zarr.json, version is a string, hierarchy version must be consistent. Missing namespace/version and mixed versions need an explicit admission policy; hard refusal versus caveated unsupported/best-effort behavior is product policy.

Conformance vocabulary, future removal of transitional metadata and JSON comment prohibition are accurate. Transitional reading may be MUST or SHOULD according to individual requirements; there is no blanket obligation that all transitional metadata readers MUST/SHOULD read every field.

Release 0.5 and draft compatibility not guaranteed are supported. Limiting this product to 0.5 is brief scope, not a universal format mandate or evidence that other releases cannot be supported. Draft rejection/best effort needs explicit product choice.

Exact existing keys and acknowledged naming exceptions must survive parsing; camelCase recommendation applies specification keys, not the viewer's arbitrary session store. Spelling difference between field_count and maximumfieldcount is not established erroneous drift.
Images are groups, each pyramid level is an array with Zarr metadata and chunks; correct Zarr v3 reading is a prerequisite. This does not by itself establish a backend's native codec coverage.

Plain images, HCS and transitional collections are grounded shapes; plate precedence over transitional collection is explicit. The complete sniff order, ambiguity UX and required all-shape breadth are proposed reader design/brief implications, not a separately stated source algorithm.
Read-only and session-local settings fit the product boundary; capture contains no reader write obligation. Read-side silence is not independent execution proof of byte preservation.

Multiple multiscales are supported and source sketches choice by name/first fallback. The report acknowledges uncertain force but promotes first fallback and voxel-count order checks into required implementation. First fallback is guidance and total voxel count is an ungrounded policy which can misjudge anisotropic resolution; capture's normative force does not depend only on uppercase keywords.

HCS plate/well hierarchy, all physical rows/columns, sparse wells, well field paths and acquisition qualifiers are grounded; listing chrome is appropriately product choice. Flat listing can preserve identity with qualifiers and is not inherently incapable.

Layout value 3, plate precedence, path-string series/OME-XML order, numbered fallback, MetadataOnly and reader SHOULD/MAY rules are accurate. Never silently first-only is a brief-driven policy, stronger than the source SHOULD; readers MAY use series, so producer requirements are not blanket reader capability mandates.

The container is not itself an image, but its contents explicitly are label images. S003 does not prohibit listing/browsing them as primary or standalone images; excluding all label subtrees is a product choice incorrectly called MUST.

Multiplicity visibility is SHOULD, and brief image-discovery acceptance supports making it an adopted requirement. Near-obligation is not a source modality and the reader may have a reasoned SHOULD exception.
Row/column and well-field identifiers have the stated alphanumeric/case-sensitive/unique rules; preserving their exact identifiers follows for correct resolution. Case-collision avoidance is SHOULD.
The source requires layout value 3 and does not explain its significance. Reject-or-flag other values is a valid product policy; capture's quotation marks do not themselves specify a string datatype.

Row groups have no separately described metadata section, but the claim that discovery is only via plate rows/wells and any directory enumeration is non-conforming overstates the source. Correct metadata validation may coexist with scanning.

Unique nonnegative acquisition ids and conditional field acquisition matching are accurate; positive counts/names/timestamps have correct producer modalities. Triple-key selection and SHOULD-show names are UI designs, not explicit spec reader mandates.

Multiple-acquisition trigger is source wording; using acquisition-list length >1 as the sole requirement trigger is an unverified implementation assumption and can miss multiple performed acquisitions when metadata is incomplete. A dangling id is invalid.

Required axes/datasets/relative paths/transforms, largest-highest-resolution-first order, matching rank/order and dimension_names are correctly stated; refusing or messaging mismatches avoids silent reinterpretation.

SHOULD contain name/type/metadata and producer fields does not mean readers SHOULD surface all those fields. Their UI display may be useful but was repeatedly promoted to source recommendations without support.

Background reads, cancellation, scoped feedback and listed malformed cases are useful plan implications. Source does not specify threading, multi-GB sizes or responsiveness architecture, and per-level recovery versus image refusal is a product policy. No actual performance evidence is present.
2-5 dimensions, 2-3 spaces, optional time/channel/custom, type order matching arrays, unique arbitrary names, matching dimension_names and conditional zyx SHOULD are accurately preserved.

Axis-driven control presence is a sound plan implication. Treating the two innermost spatial axes as the image plane is not generally justified because zyx is SHOULD and names arbitrary; custom axes need explicit semantics. Report does not expressly distinguish absent axes from present length-one axes.

Missing/custom/null type and missing/unknown units need explicit handling and cannot justify invented calibration. MUST tolerate all such input and positional slider inference are product policies, not source obligations; labeled best effort still does not establish semantic axis identity.
Array zarr.json placement is the operative precise rule. Version-history wording is imprecise shorthand, not proven contradictory dual placement. Actual validators are outside captured evidence.
omero optionality and conditional channels/color/window/min/max/start/end requirements are correct. active/coefficient/family/inverted/label/rdefs are correctly recognized as example-only.

Required presence/type of color/window fields does not establish a MUST to render them as initial color/contrast. Best-effort rdefs/active initialization is a useful product proposal; report mislabels honoring mandatory fields as a mandatory rendering algorithm.
Channel-list-size equality appears in an example comment rather than a separate MUST; overlap/default degradation is explicitly a proposed product policy.

Malformed six-hex color is covered by an explicit rule; values outside dtype/min-max or start>end have no captured normative validation rule. Calling all of them malformed format input conflicts with admitted silence; treating them as display-policy errors is valid.
Absent omero requires product-selected rendering defaults and session-local handling; a no-defaults detail message is an explicit UI proposal.

General transform vocabulary/path forms, sequential order, image-level restricted types, exactly one scale, optional one later translation, vector rank and fallback relative factors are correctly stated.

Prose correctly says dataset transforms first, then global, each listed scale before translation. Formula global(scale∘translate)∘perLevel(scale∘translate) uses ordinary composition notation in the reverse internal order. It is ambiguous/conflicting for offsets; the report gives no numerical noncommuting example to resolve it.

Worked 5D scales produce stated time/spatial spacings. Calling it a normative example is contradicted by conformance, and declaring c universally dimensionless is stronger than omission of unit in this example. Numerical calculation has no translations.

Correct composed coordinate readout is necessary within promised calibrated viewing. Mandatory display of every raw transform/name/type/extent is UI design, not an established minimum format obligation.

A scale number alone cannot establish calibration; no invented units is sound. Missing unit implies unknown declared unit, not proof that scaling is only relative. Channel axes never have meaningful physical scale is universal unsupported generalization.

Binary vectors have no detailed encoding/resolution rules in this capture; support or truthful decline is product policy. Image-group origin convention is a declared assumption, not source fact; backend resolving a vector still needs meaningful transform semantics.

Nested labels container, path-list discovery, arbitrary names/intermediate metadata-free groups, label multiscales, equal scale counts and the closed eight integer dtypes are correctly stated. Scanning unlisted labels is an explicit product decision since exhaustiveness is SHOULD.

Same-coordinate-system, usually equal dimensions/transforms, and same-or-one overview are preserved. Equal level count does not by itself prove same-index geometry; broadcasting and nearest-neighbor are justified product proposals, but warning on mismatch without establishing registration does not satisfy aligned overlay correctness.

image-label SHOULD exist and SHOULD contain colors/version; value types are MUST if keys occur. Claim version string MUST be present whenever image-label exists incorrectly promotes SHOULD to MUST. Source key is optional and image optional; accept-any-string/no-gating is a policy, not proved cross-version compatibility.

Colors SHOULD drive display, entries key by integer label-value, optional rgba has four bounded components including alpha, and properties key by label-value. Example 50% descriptions match source. Honor alpha, fallback palette, properties UI are reader/product proposals, not unconditional format mandates.

Using source.image only to annotate provenance and not to resolve actual original-image association ignores its specified relative source-image identity. The report can attach an overlay to the wrong image, especially with intermediate groups or non-parent explicit references.

Discovery/integer/count/registered geometry checks fit promised overlays; mandatory legends/properties/colors presentation exceeds source SHOULD/MAY and product choices. Association failure remains unresolved by the plan disposition.

Summary repeats validated structural obligations and misclassified color initialization/breadth/UI mandates already separately assessed; read-only is an actual brief obligation rather than a source MUST. No separate new facts are introduced.

Named producer SHOULD fields are accurately identified; displayed-field and private session camelCase recommendations are unsupported source-to-reader extensions as separately assessed. Empty groups remain possible and should not be assumed absent.

Optional keys and explicit reader choices are accurate. Optional producer metadata/global transforms cannot be ignored once relied on for calibrated viewing; custom units are tolerated through SHOULD rather than expressly MAY in cited rule.
Listed UI/performance/default/error/binary-vector policies are unresolved product choices and require product review. This classification does not authorize their unreviewed adoption elsewhere.

Sentence mapping is complete and accurately recognizes unevidenced real-tool interoperability. KEEP and EXTEND dispositions repeat earlier facts; source-derived correctness additions fit brief, but optional UI/breadth/initialization mandates and label exclusion repeat material failures above.

Most malformed versus viewer-limit versus product-boundary distinctions are useful. Unlisted labels/custom axes are allowed, optional XML can be absent, pre/post version policy is product scope, and unbounded feature claim is already contradicted. Unsupported input should be explicit, not mistaken for format invalidity.

All thirteen stated uncertainty items were checked. Genuine missing detail/implementation evidence remains unresolved; total-voxel metric, universal no-calibration from no-unit, source-association handling and imposed accept-any-version do not gain source authority by being recorded as assumptions.

There is no supplied worked example with translated multiaxis composition; supplied example has both global time and dataset spatial scaling. Beyond time is imprecise, but no offset numerical oracle is provided.

Count fields overlap but equality is not established; display-hints-only is a proposal. Alleged editorial duplicate by the by the is not literally in source; source repeats by across adjacent lines, no consequence for semantics.

V1-V9 are explicitly UNEXECUTED proposals, not fabricated execution evidence. They cover named positive/negative paths, read-only and performance; adoption of unsupported rendering/default policies within test expectations remains a proposal, not source validation.

Proposed coordinate tests use scale-only worked values and generic translation handling; there is no explicit numerical fixture that distinguishes dataset translation later globally scaled from reversed composition. This is a coverage omission, not a false execution claim.

Proposed label tests omit exact uint64/int64 identity and explicit source-association rejection/verification despite integer/dtype enumeration. Alignment mismatch warnings alone do not demonstrate correct association.
Source locator index was checked against all cited sections. It adds no independent material assertions beyond rule descriptions already assessed; cited sections exist and topic ranges are accurate.
Global assertion that all findings are S003-supported is false given material unsupported/contradicted statements; unresolved-area and UNEXECUTED qualifications do not erase those current mandates.

facets.decision: Explicit Zarr v3, ome namespace, consistent version and unsupported/best-effort admission policy; no implicit legacy reinterpretation is promised.

Rank/order/name/dimension_names checks and variable dimension control presence are covered. Absent versus present length-one axes is not explicit; two-innermost-plane and positional custom slider assumptions leave semantic identity unsupported.

Metadata order, arbitrary group-relative paths, per-level transforms and explicit missing/malformed level feedback are covered; no fixed factor formula is authoritative. Voxel-count sanity metric is an additional unsupported policy already flagged.

Both transform tiers and no-invented-unit caveat are covered, but notation reverses internal composition and concrete worked test has no translations/noncommuting offsets. Generic translation proposal does not expose that failure.

Declared labels paths, intermediate groups, level count and geometry are covered. Explicit policy treats source.image only as provenance, so original-image association is not validated before overlay.

Integer/categorical and non-interpolating label handling plus label-value metadata semantics are recognized, and colors remain SHOULD. No exact integer decoding/lookup range or refusal for unsupported uint64/int64 precision is defined.
